ai.description: *Cantoria violacea* reaches 1 meter in length. It is dark grey or black with distinct yellow crossbands and a pale belly. The head is small, and the body is slender with smooth, glossy scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cantoria violacea* is best distinguished by its unique pattern of 30–40 narrow, pale yellow crossbars on a dark body, which remain distinct throughout its entire length.
ai.habitat: *Cantoria violacea* inhabits intertidal mangrove forests and muddy estuarine banks within the Indian subcontinent, typically occurring at or near sea level.
ai.behavior: *Cantoria violacea* is a nocturnal specialist that hunts mudskippers by waiting patiently in mangrove burrows during low tide to ambush its prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cantoria violacea* is viviparous, producing small litters of 2–4 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cantoria violacea* is found in the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans in West Bengal, India, typically occurring at or near sea level.
